newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire PM reiterates no talks till Rwandan's leave.
newsitem.headline: Zaire PM reiterates no talks till Rwandan's leave.

text.p: Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo reiterated in an interview on Saturday with Belgian radio broadcast that there was no question of negotiating with Rwanda until it withdrew from Zaire's territory.
"I will not meet the Rwandan's as long as they are on our territory," Kengo told RTBF radio.
In the past week Zairean and Rwandan troops have fired at one another across their border at the two main Rwandan towns, Gisenyi and Cyangugu.
Rwanda has admitted sending troops into Zaire on a military sortie earlier this week, and on Saturday Rwandan troops attacked the town of Goma.
The Rwandan troops had thrust into Goma the previous day by lake and land after mortar and machinegun exchanges with Zairean troops, diplomats said.
Asked how the conflict could be ended Kengo said, "First of all there has to be a ceasefire. The troops on our territory have to leave, then we can negotiate."

He said the question of the mainly Hutu Rwandan refugees in Zaire, more than a million of whom are caught up in fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean soldiers and militiamen, had to be resolved, and they must return to their own country.
"One would say that the Rwandans don't want to share power with the refugees, but they are Rwandans too," he added.
